citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bemstein, M. S., & Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv preprint arXiv:1602.07332.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei (Stanford University, Dresden University of Technology, Yahoo Inc., Snapchat Inc.)
description: A dataset of images densely annotated with numerous region descriptions, objects, attributes, and relationships to enable the modeling of such relationships and cognitive understanding of images.
name: Visual Genome
rai:annotationsPerItem: An average of 42 region descriptions per image (50 collected), 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs per image.
rai:annotatorDemographics: The majority of workers were between the ages of 25 and 34 years old (youngest 18, oldest 68). Near-balanced split of 54.15% male and 45.85% female workers. 93.02% of workers contributed from the United States.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All Visual Genome data go through a verification stage using majority voting (three unique workers looking at each annotation and voting on whether it is factually correct; added if at least two verify) and rapid judgments for objects.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers are asked to draw bounding boxes and write descriptions for regions, ensuring coverage and quality. Objects, attributes, and relationships are then extracted from these descriptions. Bounding boxes must cover all objects mentioned and be as tight as possible. Questions and answers are written following rules to start with one of the 'seven Ws', avoid ambiguity, and be precise.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. Certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) are overrepresented due to a bias towards these sports in the images.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of 108,249 images from the intersection of MS-COCO's 328,000 images and YFCC's 100 million images. Annotations were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world, non-iconic images that were uploaded onto Flickr by users.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs are canonicalized to their respective synsets in the WordNet ontology. Stanford NLP tools are used to extract noun phrases.
rai:dataUseCases: Image search, question answering, robotic interactions, semantic image retrieval, dense image captioning, relationship extraction.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford's dependency parser was used to extract nouns automatically and send them to the workers as suggestions. Word2vec was used for semantic clustering.
